correctness.rationale: The polygon has at most one side per prism face, hence at most n+2. Away from planes through a vertex, with q=|U_z| and t=hq/√(1−q²), the top and bottom each contribute two crossed edges if t is below the maximum absolute horizontal vertex projection, and none above it. The n vertical edges occur in opposite pairs, a pair crossing exactly if its projection modulus is below t. Thus the n+2 event is exactly that t lies between the two largest moduli. Folding the azimuth onto (0,π/n) gives those moduli as cos φ and cos(2π/n−φ); Haar q is independent uniform on (0,1). The CDF b/√(h²+b²) and elementary antiderivative give exactly the stated probability, also for n=4. The derivative in z=(1+h²)^−1/2 has sign 1−3 cos²(π/n) z² after comparison of positive radicals; the unique zero is interior even at n=4. Substitution, the cubic Taylor term 2(π/n)^3/(3√3) in the arcsine difference, and the exact square and hexagon evaluations agree with the finding. The supplied Monte Carlo/quadrature code was inspected, not rerun, and is not needed for the proof.
